evidence.reading: context.rs is the L1 generation store's constructor module. Under the External scheme (build_stochastic_context branches at lines 675-681, 717-740, 747-766) it reaches into System's realized-value external-scenario tables (external_scenarios / external_load_scenarios / external_ncs_scenarios) and synthesizes fitted InflowModel/LoadModel from their sample moments, and it reimplements cobre-io's declared-id->study-index resolver (StageIdResolver, verified live at crates/cobre-io/src/lib.rs:142 + ~8 call sites) because the L1 crate cannot depend on the L2 crate. This is the Q2 generation-vs-realized straddle: the fitted-process seam owns realized-value adaptation and a second copy of stage-id resolution. Not a dispute of the ratified External-authoritative behavior (mirror L983) nor the sigma=0 rejection; strictly a placement/coupling observation. The moment derivation itself is single-owner (derive_external_sample_moments, sampling/external.rs) and correctly shared, so drift risk is confined to stage_id_to_index vs StageIdResolver and to the ingestion glue's home.

candidates.fixShape: Roadmap-aligned: under Part-1 purification the external-scenario tables leave `System` for the cobre-stochastic uncertainty store; the External-ingestion adaptation (sample-moment -> fitted-model synthesis) then moves WITH those tables into the store rather than living in the context constructor, and the paradigm-neutral declared-id->study-index resolver homes once at L0 (cobre-core temporal, the same destination the mirror already registers for the season_cast relocation) so this crate (L1) and cobre-io (L2) consume one resolver instead of two parallel implementations. No engine noun and no L1->engine dependency is introduced. As a bounded interim step short of purification, extract the four External-ingestion helpers (stage_id_to_index, resolve_row_stages, external_derived_load_models, external_ar0_inflow_models) into their own submodule so the store constructor is not the owner of realized-value adaptation.

candidates.title: StochasticContext is both a computed store and a config/layout echo: 5 precomputed components + 5 derived-layout scalars + 2 pass-through seeds + 1 metadata field, each exposed via a 1:1 &-getter (the nascent Switchable<T> uncertainty store)

evidence.output: 257: #[derive(Debug)] 258: pub struct StochasticContext { 259:     par_lp: PrecomputedPar, 260:     correlation: DecomposedCorrelation, 261:     opening_tree: OpeningTree, 262:     normal_lp: PrecomputedNormal, 263:     ncs_normal: PrecomputedNormal, 264:     ncs_entity_ids: Vec<EntityId>, 265:     entity_order: Box<[EntityId]>, 266:     base_seed: u64, 270:     forward_seed: Option<u64>, 271:     dim: usize, 272:     n_load_buses: usize, 273:     n_stochastic_ncs: usize, 274:     provenance: StochasticProvenance, 275: }
evidence.reading: The 13 private fields split into four roles: 5 precomputed components (par_lp, correlation, opening_tree, normal_lp, ncs_normal) that ARE the store; 5 derived-layout values (ncs_entity_ids, entity_order, dim, n_load_buses, n_stochastic_ncs) that are addressing metadata recomputable from noise_entity_order; 2 pass-through config values (base_seed, forward_seed) echoed straight from the builder args; and 1 metadata field (provenance). Every field is surfaced through a trivial &-returning getter (par()/correlation()/opening_tree()/normal()/ncs_normal()/entity_order()/... at 285-393); the only real behavior is set_solve_order (line 317), a post-construction mutation of the opening tree (two-phase init). So the Q3 answer is BOTH: a store (the precomputed infra, read by ~30 downstream files across cobre-sddp/cli, so NOT a one-consumer abstraction) fused with a parameter/layout bag (config echoed back through getters). Q4 hint: the precomputed-component group is the Switchable<T> store payload; the derived-layout group is its addressing metadata; base_seed/forward_seed are RunParams-shaped and separate from the store under the input-data-lifecycle split.

candidates.fixShape: Phase-1 destination note, NOT executed by this spec (lens Q4 is alignmentHint-only). No restructuring here; recorded so the alignment epic knows this struct is the carve target and the config-echo/store fusion is the seam to unpick.
